# 詩總聞

**ID:** KR1c0014
**Custom ID:** ZB1c0008
**Date (file):** 2015-08-24 22:04:40.298814
**Source:** 四庫全書 文淵閣版, V72.2, p433
**Extent:** 20 卷
**Base edition:** WYG

## Authors / Editors
- 王質 (宋朝) 撰 1127 - 1189

**Editions:** WYG

## Summary (Ask Bunkankun 聞分館君)

A 20-*juǎn* commentary on all 305 odes, organized by a distinctive ten-fold "hearing" (*wén* 聞) scheme. For each ode Wáng Zhì gives a discussion of its general meaning, then runs the ode through ten *wén* categories: *wén yīn* 聞音 (sound), *wén xùn* 聞訓 (philological gloss), *wén zhāng* 聞章 (stanzas), *wén jù* 聞句 (lines), *wén zì* 聞字 (graphs), *wén wù* 聞物 (things), *wén yòng* 聞用 (function), *wén jì* 聞跡 (historical traces), *wén zhuān* 聞專 (special points), and *wén rén* 聞人 (persons). Each ode receives a final *zǒngwén* 總聞 ("comprehensive hearing"). At the head of the four *shǐ* 始 sections he places three further section-introductions — *wén Fēng* 聞風, *wén Yǎ* 聞雅, *wén Sòng* 聒頌 — surveying the genre as a whole. Like Zhèng Qiáo 鄭樵 ([KR1c0019](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR1/KR1c/KR1c0019)) and Zhū Xī ([KR1c0009](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR1/KR1c/KR1c0009) / [KR1c0015](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR1/KR1c/KR1c0015)), Wáng Zhì rejects the *small preface* — but unlike Zhèng he does not attack it openly, and unlike Zhū he does not develop a rival doctrinal frame. He simply ignores it and reads the poems on their own terms.

**Abstract**

The *Shī zǒngwén* is the Southern-Sòng *Shī* commentary that comes closest, in spirit, to a fully secular reading of the *Classic of Poetry*: the ten-*wén* analytical scheme is in effect a structural-philological and historical methodology that treats each ode as a self-standing object. Composition spans roughly thirty years (Wáng Zhì's own statement) ending with his death in 1189; circulation began with Chén Rìqiáng's 1243 Fùchuān edition, after which the work was nearly lost (the *Sìkù* editors trace its preservation through the Míng-Qīng book trade — Xiè Zhàozhè → Chén Kāizhòng → Zhōu Liànggōng). The Sìkù editors themselves rate it more highly than Zhèng Qiáo's *Shī biàn wàng* ([KR1c0019](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR1/KR1c/KR1c0019)) precisely because it abstains from open attack on the *xù* and concentrates on positive philological reading. The dating bracket is set from the *jìnshì* date (1160, when Wáng Zhì begins his official career and the thirty-year project plausibly starts) to his death (1189).
